crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Drafting a Manuscript
children.blurb: Drafting a manuscript is the stage of research writing where findings, methods and prior work are assembled into a single document intended for peer review and publication.

children.name: Testing Arguments Before Peer Review
children.blurb: Testing arguments before peer review is the practice of checking a paper's reasoning, evidence and internal consistency while the manuscript is still in the author's hands, rather than waiting for referees to find the gaps.

children.name: Disciplinary Register and Language
children.blurb: Disciplinary register and language covers the conventions of vocabulary, tone, hedging and structure that mark a text as belonging to a particular field.

children.name: Plagiarism and AI Detection
children.blurb: Plagiarism and AI detection covers the tools and practices used to judge whether a piece of writing was copied from an existing source or produced by a generative model.

children.name: Explaining Research After Publication
children.blurb: Explaining research after publication covers the work of translating a finished paper for readers who will not read the paper itself: press releases, plain language summaries, blog posts, thread write ups, and talks.

sections.body: Academic writing and peer review is the part of research practice where a study becomes a manuscript, gets tested by reviewers, and then reaches readers. Artificial intelligence now sits at most stages of that pipeline. It drafts sections, suggests related work, checks whether an argument holds together, flags passages that resemble existing text, and helps rewrite a paper for a journal or a general audience. The work is not theoretical. Researchers use these tools on real submissions, real revision letters and real press summaries, and the tools are embedded in the same documents that go out under a human author's name.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some tasks are genuinely useful and some are not. Language polishing, reference formatting and producing a plain summary of a finished study are largely solved, and the output is often good enough to edit rather than rewrite. Argument testing is partly solved, in that a model can point out a missing control or an unsupported leap, but it cannot judge whether a claim is true. Plagiarism and AI detection remain unreliable, with false positives on ordinary academic prose and false negatives on lightly edited text, so a detection score is not evidence of misconduct. Originality checking against a real corpus is more dependable than guessing authorship, and this site holds 15,047 claims extracted from research works, which is the kind of structured material such checks need. The honest limit is that no tool here decides whether a paper is correct, novel or worth publishing, and reviewers still carry that judgment.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages follow the life of a manuscript in order. Drafting a Manuscript covers turning notes and results into a submission, including structure, figures and the first full pass.Disciplinary Register and Language deals with writing that sounds like the field rather than like a chatbot, which matters most in fields with strict conventions. Plagiarism and AI Detection explains what similarity tools can and cannot show, and why a match score needs a human reading before anyone draws a conclusion. Explaining Research After Publication takes the finished paper outward to readers who will never open the methods section, and it is the page to visit once the work is accepted rather than before.
